Scope: arterial and local roads, potable water, sewage, storm drainage, irrigation, street lighting and telecom networks, sewage pump stations and storm drainage ponds for Phase 1, Part 2 of the 3rd Industrial City in Dammam.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours, on the same basis as last week: the 2,336,000 budgeted labour units of MODON's revised schedule, including engineering, procurement and testing. At the 15-Nov-2026 data date the project is 43.5% complete, up from 42.2% last week, against 58.3% planned, 14.8% behind plan. Most of this week's gain came from procurement; construction moved by only 0.2%.

The P6 update now finishes the project 176 days late. The contractor's P6 update (data date 14-Nov-2026) schedules project finish on 10-Nov-2027, 176 days after the contract completion date of 18-May-2027 and 7 days later than last week, with −175 days of float; it records no progress at all since last week. The weekly report and MODON's revised schedule still show 18-May-2027. To finish on the contract date, the remaining 56.5% needs about 2.17% a week over the 26 whole weeks left; this week gained 1.26%, of which 1.12% was one procurement activity (water pumps delivery) and 0.13% construction. Construction stands at 52.7% against 78.8% planned.

Site photos this week

Six of the twelve site photos uploaded with this week's report, stamped 14 to 17 November 2026 by the contractor's camera app. Work covered manhole leak testing and pipe connections, hand excavation for a pipe sleeve, power cabling at the pump stations and for the street lighting, and insulation of valves after the hydrostatic test. The schedules uploaded this week disagree on completion. The contractor's P6 update (1,255 activities, data date 14-Nov-2026) finishes on 10-Nov-2027, 7 days later than last week's 03-Nov-2027, because its data date moved a week without any progress being recorded. MODON's revised schedule "MDD-Update 79" (2,970 activities, data date still 09-Nov-2026), which carries the physical measure, finishes on 18-May-2027 with no float to spare and the revised-scope works on 03-Apr-2027. The P6 export in the weekly report's Milestones sheet shows 11-Jul-2027, and the weekly report itself forecasts 18-May-2027.

Procurement of key materials

Share of total quantity delivered to site for the long-lead items. Source: procurement log, Procurement status sheet, updated this week.

Pumps: 2 of 15 deliveredGrundfos pump accessories are being installed at the stations, but only 2 pumps have arrived because of global shipping problems; no pump or panel was delivered this week. The water station control panel (IGEC, 1 set) is expected in January 2027, and its delivery is now tied to the contractor's financial claim. The sewage station panels (WAMCO, 4 sets) are reported as partly supplied, with full delivery in January 2027, but none is counted as delivered.
Generators and surge vesselsThe two generators (Kohler – Abunayyan) are in the Kingdom and wait for the factory and site acceptance tests before delivery to site. The surge vessel supplier (7 units) has written to warn of late delivery because of shipping conditions in the region; the expected date is 28-Nov-2026. The VEGA supplier has given no delivery date, and the water pump maintenance (SPP) expects its parts on 24-Nov-2026.

Labour has fallen from 397 in March–April to 332; the MODON issue log names low manpower and productivity as a cause of delay. The sheet records 114 items of equipment for November.

Long-lead suppliesContractorSome long-lead supplies are late because of regional and global shipping problems (high risk): 2 of 15 pumps delivered, control panels due in January 2027, and the surge vessel supplier has notified a delay. Action: follow up purchase orders and deliveries.
Manpower and productivityContractorLow manpower and low productivity of the contractor's crews (MODON issue log, high priority). Action: increase manpower and raise productivity.
Hand excavationContractorExcavation is done by hand because there are no records of the existing services, which lengthens the works. Action: trial pits before excavation to confirm there are no existing lines.

Data notes

  • This-week values compare with the 10-Nov-2026 upload in the W07 folder (data date 08-Nov-2026) and its schedule MDD-Update 78. No weekly presentation was uploaded this week, so the network quantities, the presentation's issues and the executed-but-not-invoiced figures are not available. The procurement log file name still carries 20-Oct-2026, but its contents were updated.
  • The report week is the contract week stated in the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 78 of 104"); (15-Nov-2026 − 19-May-2025) ÷ 7 gives 77 whole weeks, as contract weeks count from 1. The workbook still calls itself report #65, as last week, and its file name carries 11-17-2026 (17-Nov-2026, month first) although its data date is 15-Nov-2026.
  • The workbook has gone back to the old measure: the Weekly Progress Report, Progress and Physical-Chart Data sheets again count construction man-hours only (458,486 and 467,280) and show 77.8% against 96.8% planned. To stay on last week's basis, this report takes the actual from MODON's revised schedule MDD-Update 79 (the "REV002" schedule file): 1,015,605 earned of 2,336,000 budgeted labour units (43.5%), against 986,227 (42.2%) in MDD-Update 78, the same figure the weekly report showed last week.
  • MDD-Update 79 still carries the data date 09-Nov-2026 of Update 78, although its progress has moved on. Of the 29,377 labour units gained, 26,270 are one procurement activity ("Water Pumps DOS"); construction gained 3,107.
  • The new Revised schedule sheet of the weekly report ("Modon Revised - Update 9-11-26") gives 58.3% planned and 39.5% earned (922,788 units). It leaves pre-testing and testing at zero, although the schedule shows 71,796 units earned, and counts procurement as 114,623 earned units against 135,644 in the schedule. Its plan is used here because no other plan on the new basis was uploaded; as it leaves out pre-testing and testing, the real plan is higher and the SPI lower than shown.
  • Last week's Weekly Progress Report sheet showed no earned units for the Zone 3 main road; MDD-Update 78 had 95.6% (now 99.9%).
  • The contractor's P6 update (data date 14-Nov-2026) is unchanged from last week's apart from the data date: no activity status or % complete changed, so every forecast moved 7 days later. It still leaves milestones 3 and 4 (work plan, drawings approval) not started, while the weekly report shows them complete. The Schedule sheet's activity counts (543 not started, 334 in progress, 378 completed) do not match the P6 update file (345, 422, 488).
  • Completion dates disagree: weekly report 18-May-2027; MDD-Update 79 18-May-2027; P6 export in the Milestones sheet 11-Jul-2027; contractor's P6 update 10-Nov-2027.
  • The earned value columns of the workbook and the cost table of the Revised schedule sheet report value-weighted (cost-based) progress labelled as achieved; those figures are not used in this report.
  • Contract value: the revised contract value cell of the Weekly Progress Report sheet is blank (146,170,171 SAR last week); the Revised schedule sheet gives 164,170,172 SAR for the revised scope and 69,605,906 SAR of saving scope. The Invoice Log shows unexplained figures of 21,100,000 (revised contract value), 20,900,000 (estimate at completion) and 200,000 (potential changes).
  • Invoices: the Invoice Log now records payment of all 14 progress invoices (65,141,130 SAR) and the advance payment, while its summary and the Weekly Progress Report sheet still count 4 paid invoices (15,540,346 SAR) and 10 pending. Invoice 8 is shown paid on 01-Mar-2025, before its own period (20-Jan to 15-Feb-2026).
